chunks.content: # The Designer's CLO Journey: Awakening Summer Pet Clothing Making Tutorial This document details the step-by-step process of designing and simulating a 3D pet clothing model using CLO software. It covers virtual pet model setup, panel creation, 3D modeling techniques, pocket and collar design, hat construction, strap and lining application, fabric and color management, sewing and simulation adjustments, and final rendering. --- ## Setting Up the Virtual Pet Model in CLO This section explains how to import and prepare a virtual puppy model in CLO for pet clothing design, including background adjustments and initial 3D modeling tool usage. - Open CLO and access the library window. - Import a pre-constructed virtual puppy model, available for free download via CONNECT. - Drag and drop the puppy model into CLO and open it. - Modify the background to improve visibility of the model. - The clothing design includes division structures, a three-dimensional pocket, and a cover. - Use the 3D model tool to begin drawing: - Switch to the fifth angle for better perspective. - Draw straight lines by holding the Shift key; double-click to finish lines. - Position the collar line using the CTRL key. - Use left-click to start and end lines, double-click to confirm. - Adjust points and curves with the Embedded 3D Pen Tool for precision. - Draw the front center line, background curves, and front leg curves using the Ctrl key for curve positioning. - Diagonal lines on side abdomen, waist, back thigh (with curves), and shoulder improve garment fit and texture suitability. --- ## Creating and Optimizing Panels This section describes the process of creating garment panels, optimizing curves, merging panels, and preparing for simulation. - Use the flat-screen tool to select all panels while holding Shift; press Enter to open panels. - Quickly clean and adjust panel directions. - Right-click panels and use the optimization curve tool to smooth curves and reduce complexity; set a suitable optimization percentage. - Expand panels by 105% for appropriate garment volume. - Duplicate panels (Ctrl+D), reposition using the position ball. - Merge overlapping back panels using the edit panel tool: - Select panel outlines, right-click, and choose Merge. - Delete unnecessary curve points before merging. - Use edit point tool to adjust curves post-merge. - Temporarily merge back lines and open simulation to adjust garment fit. - Harden simulation and adjust bottom curves as needed. --- ## Designing the Collar This section covers precise collar panel creation, measurement, and positioning on the puppy model. - Select two lines using Shift key; total length measured at 190.9 mm. - Create a curved collar panel: width 191 mm, height 60 mm. - Use the extension panel line tool to extend line 1 by 160 mm. - Align the collar panel on the model using the positioning ball. - Cull border lines and seams as necessary for clean edges. - Harden and run simulation on the collar panel. - Remove temporary lines using the edgable panel line tool.

average section measures 40 mm. - Create shape with internal shape tool: - Temperature: 20 mm - Height: 21 mm - Length and width of arms: 2.2 mm - Height of arm: 7 mm - Align shapes using adjustment board tool; stack rectangles in the same position. - Use line sewing tool to sew lines and simulate. - Use inner circle tool to create string holes: - Diameter: 14 mm - Angle: 180 degrees - Positioned 28 mm above, 22 mm left - Convert circles to holes; lock and unlock panels as necessary. - Use tie string tool to simulate string threading and bending. - Adjust bending rate for realistic effect. --- ## Managing Pocket Panels and Strap Construction This section covers panel separation, freezing, hardening, and detailed editing to avoid fabric piercing and ensure structural integrity. - Select and drag pocket panels outward; reverse-activate related sewing lines. - Hide large panels and freeze pocket panels. - Harden strap panels and adjust model attributes: - Set force of force value to 0.1 for touch sensitivity.

reverse-activate related sewing lines. - Hide large panels and freeze pocket panels. - Harden strap panels and adjust model attributes: - Set force of force value to 0.1 for touch sensitivity. - Use the multilayer line tool to draw built-in lines; divide lines evenly. - Cut and delete excess panels along division lines. - Sew ends in the 3D window and simulate. - Adjust pocket panel thickness to 1 mm for conflict resolution. - Flatten strap panels and match them with large strap panels without piercing. - Freeze and simulate to ensure panel stability. --- ## Creating and Simulating the Hat This section explains how to design a pet hat, including circle creation, panel arrangement, pinning, and detailed simulation for fit. - Use the round tool to create a 210 mm diameter circle. - Apply inner circle tool; position the hat on the model’s head using the positioning ball. - Harden and repeatedly simulate to adjust fit. - Ensure circle orientation matches window directions. - Add fixed pins around the hat panel edges using the fixed pin comparison tool. - Position pins naturally under the dog’s ears. - Remove pins after natural fit is confirmed. - Use the flat-tip tool and optimization point tool to clean unnecessary line points. - Adjust curves and symmetry using the selection tool. - Sew hat panels and edges together with matching sewing lines. - Harden and simulate; adjust shape for symmetrical effect. --- ## Hat Rope and Lining Application This section describes creating the hat rope with multilinear lines, arranging it near the neck, and adding lining for structure. - Use internal multilinear line tool to create 3 mm wide lines. - Use rectangular selection tool to create 250 mm x 3 mm rectangles. - Arrange ropes near the dog’s neck with the quick array tool. - Freeze eye area, sew ropes, and remove fixing pins for natural fall. - Add fixing pins selectively and manually adjust rope closeness. - Add lining: - Import lining from CONNECT. - Set lining width to 10 mm with fixed proportion. - Position lining using the positioning ball. - Add fixing pins along sewing lines and simulate. - Remove pins after stabilization. - Freeze sewing lines. - Select multiple linings on the head, make them more rigid and simulate. --- ## Mask and Double-Layer Effect This section covers mask creation with inner line borders, rendering thickness, and double-layer garment effects. - Add internal line borders on mask lines; set border size to 10 mm and 4 units for mask. - Add rendering thickness of 2 mm. - Enable double-layer effect for mask. - Freeze mask and pocket effects after activation.

set border size to 10 mm and 4 units for mask. - Add rendering thickness of 2 mm. - Enable double-layer effect for mask. - Freeze mask and pocket effects after activation. - Select shell layers and fill them to create double-layer effects. --- ## Adding Stickers and Embroidery Labels This section explains how to add sticker materials, position them, and create embroidery labels on the clothing. - Add shared sticker material to the physical window. - Place and rotate the sticker on the desired location. - Use inner shape of shell layer for sticker positioning. - Lock outlines and convert points to free horizon points for neat edges. - Optimize horizontal points with adjustment panel tool (50% optimization). - Add sticker to outside and simulate. - Adjust sticker thickness to 2 mm and scale to 40%. - Remove unused sticker versions. - Create small embroidery labels on the hat by copying, shrinking, and positioning. - Use positioning tool for precise size adjustment. --- ## Designing Shoulder and Back Straps This section describes measuring, creating, sewing, and simulating shoulder and back straps with foldable edges and accessory hooks. - Measure shoulder strap length (~35.9 cm). - Create shape-shape with width 15 cm and height 40 mm. - Divide upper and lower parts with add line tool. - Sew on the large sheet using free sewing tool. - Set upper edge as foldable; lower edge as normal seam. - Simulate and sew strap to the body. - Add internal line on shoulder to fold inward; fold angle ~90 degrees. - Use Ctrl+D to align the opposite shoulder flat. - For the long back strap: - Measure length (~123 cm) and width (15 mm). - Draw internal center line and delete one side for symmetry. - Sew the remaining side; top and bottom seams are flat. - Add 30 mm points on top and bottom lines using add line tool. - Draw parallel internal lines along these points. - Sew terminal lines to concentrate extra length
